name: Head Start and Early Head Start (service-area grants)
what: Head Start grants pay a local agency to run preschool (Head Start) and infant-toddler (Early Head Start) programmes for low-income children and families in a defined service area [1251](#cite:1251). An agency is designated for five years at a time; under the Designation [Renewal](#term:renewal) System it is either renewed without competition or made to compete for its next five-year grant [1226](#cite:1226). A new applicant can apply only when a service area is put out for competition [1229](#cite:1229). On 2026-10-04 no notice was open and one multi-state notice was [forecast](#term:forecast) for FY2027 [1227](#cite:1227) [1251](#cite:1251).

who_may_apply.limits: A non-Indian agency may run an Indian Head Start programme only until an Indian Head Start agency becomes available and is designated [1226](#cite:1226).
who_may_apply.eligibility_note: A non-profit that is not a university may apply. The Office of Head Start names local public or private non-profit organisations, including faith-based organisations, and local for-profit organisations in the community [1229](#cite:1229). Individuals, sole proprietorships and foreign entities are not eligible [1251](#cite:1251). An agency whose Head Start grant was [terminated](#term:termination) for cause, or which was denied refunding, in the preceding five years may not compete [1226](#cite:1226).

steps: Register for a [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei), in [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) and in [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov) at least one month before the notice opens [1229](#cite:1229).
Watch the Office of Head Start [NOFO](#term:nofo) locator and Grants.gov for the service areas open for competition [1227](#cite:1227).
Apply through Grants.gov under the notice for the service area; the application must show the applicant is the most qualified entity to deliver the programme [1227](#cite:1227) [1226](#cite:1226).
owner: Administration for Children and Families, Office of Head Start (HHS)
service_area: Each notice names the service areas open. The FY2027 forecast covers areas in 37 states and territories, from Alabama to Wisconsin and including the Virgin Islands [1251](#cite:1251). Service areas come open when a grantee relinquishes or loses its grant or meets a Designation Renewal condition [1229](#cite:1229).

cycle.pattern: Not a fixed annual competition. Seven conditions in 45 [CFR](#term:cfr) 1304.11 send an existing agency into competition: two or more deficiencies; school readiness goals not set or used; CLASS Pre-K scores below the thresholds (Emotional Support below 5, Classroom Organization below 5, Instructional Support below 2.3 through July 31, 2027 and below 2.5 after August 1, 2027); licence revocation; suspension; debarment or disqualification from the Child and Adult Care Food Program; and fiscal risk [1226](#cite:1226). [ACF](#term:acf) tells an agency at least 12 months before its grant ends whether it must compete [1226](#cite:1226). The last service-area notice found on Grants.gov was posted February 27, 2025 and closed April 29, 2025; no service-area notice was posted between then and the September 2, 2026 forecasts [1250](#cite:1250).

current_notices.note: Forecast only, posted September 2, 2026 and updated September 16, 2026; both dates are estimates. Estimated award date July 30, 2027 and estimated start August 2, 2027 [1251](#cite:1251).

match: Federal money may not exceed 80 percent of approved total programme costs; the grantee contributes 20 percent as non-federal match each [budget period](#term:budget-period) unless the HHS official approves a waiver [1249](#cite:1249).
cost_sharing: Required: a 20 percent non-federal match (45 CFR 1303.4) [1249](#cite:1249).
budget_rules: Costs to develop and administer the programme may not exceed 15 percent of total approved programme costs unless a waiver is granted [1249](#cite:1249).
review: Non-federal objective review panels, typically three reviewers and a chairperson, score applications against the criteria in the notice. Common criteria are demonstration of need, early learning and development outcomes, past performance, staffing, planning and implementation, organisational capacity and governance, and budget. Scores and rankings do not bind ACF, which also weighs management and financial record and the geographic distribution of funds. ACF states that about four to six months pass between receipt and award [1228](#cite:1228).
distinctive: The grant is a designation for a place, not a project award: ACF describes the Designation Renewal System as the way it decides whether an agency delivers high-quality services and qualifies for five more years [1226](#cite:1226).

what: The Basic Center Program pays community organisations to give runaway and homeless youth under 18 up to 21 days of emergency shelter, with food, clothing, counselling, referrals for health care and aftercare [1238](#cite:1238) [1234](#cite:1234). Non-profits with and without [501(c)(3)](#term:section-501c3) status are listed, and faith-based and community organisations that meet the requirements are eligible. Priority goes to entities with experience serving runaway and homeless youth [1234](#cite:1234). Applicants must show experience running similar programmes, and a shelter must be licensed where state or local law requires it [1235](#cite:1235).

steps: Register in [SAM.gov](#term:sam-gov) (which issues the [Unique Entity Identifier](#term:uei)) and in [Grants.gov](#term:grants-gov), which needs a [Login.gov](#term:login-gov) account [1235](#cite:1235).

name: Family Violence Prevention and Services Act formula grants to states and tribes
what: The Family Violence Prevention and Services Act sends [formula grants](#term:formula-grant) to states, territories and tribes for shelter and supportive services for victims of domestic violence; the local programmes that deliver the services are funded by those grantees [1243](#cite:1243). The office reports that FVPSA-funded local programmes gave 16,993,979 shelter nights in 2024 [1243](#cite:1243). The same Act also funds state domestic violence coalitions, resource centres and specialised services through separate lines [1243](#cite:1243).

who_may_apply.eligibility_note: A local non-profit does not apply to [ACF](#term:acf) for formula funds. The federal [grant](#term:grant) goes to the state, territory or tribe [1243](#cite:1243). A [subgrant](#term:subaward) may go to a local public agency or a non-profit private organisation, including faith-based and charitable organisations, community-based organisations, tribal organisations and voluntary associations [1355](#cite:1355). Of the funds a state distributes, not less than 70 percent goes to entities whose primary purpose is immediate shelter and not less than 25 percent to supportive and prevention services [1355](#cite:1355).

owner: Administration for Children and Families, Office of Family Violence Prevention and Services (HHS)
pass_through_via: The state or territory agency, or the tribe, that receives the FVPSA formula grant [1243](#cite:1243).

cycle.pattern: Annual formula allotment; no competition for the formula grants. The [appropriation](#term:appropriations-act) for Family Violence Prevention and Services was $240,000 thousand in FY2025 and $245,000 thousand in FY2026, with $245,000 thousand requested for FY2027 [1339](#cite:1339). name: Community Services Block Grant
what: CSBG is a block grant to states, territories and tribes [1239](#cite:1239). name: Older Americans Act Title III - supportive services, nutrition and caregiver support
what: Older Americans Act money for home and community-based services, congregate and home-delivered meals and family caregiver support is [formula funding](#term:formula-grant). It passes from [ACL](#term:acl) to 56 [state agencies on aging](#term:state-administering-agency), then to 618 area agencies on aging, then to nearly 20,000 local service providers [1260](#cite:1260). ACL describes formula grants as ongoing programmes that need no application or competition [1259](#cite:1259).

who_may_apply.eligibility_note: A non-profit does not apply to ACL for [Title III](#term:title-iii-v-eligibility) funds. Title VI [grants](#term:grant) go to Indian Tribal Organizations [1260](#cite:1260).

owner: Administration for Community Living, Administration on Aging (HHS)
pass_through_via: The state agency on aging and the area agency on aging for the planning and service area [1260](#cite:1260) [1261](#cite:1261).
